manifest.notes:
This is a beta version, published only on the beta update channel. It brings two new sections with the Beta
mark: Microsoft 365, which connects each company's Microsoft 365 to view and manage people, mailboxes, groups and
licenses, with automations, policies and backups of mailboxes, OneDrive and SharePoint; and Security awareness,
with simulated phishing campaigns against your own staff, short courses and a button to report. It also brings Backups
fixes and improvements, the departments rule in more places and a safer Linux installer.

Before updating, make a backup and keep it (Administration › System & updates › Backups). This version adds
tables to the database, and that backup is the safe way back (see "Keep in mind" at the end). A server on the stable
channel is not offered this version: to get it, choose the beta channel in
Administration › System & updates › Updates.

The Beta mark means the same as in 1.8.4: the feature works and you can use it as usual, but it has not passed
final verification yet, so some details may still change. It is only a notice: it doesn't limit anything or change how
the feature behaves. Microsoft 365 and Security awareness haven't been tested with a real tenant yet: start with a
test company (see "Keep in mind"). The "Beta features" help article shows where the mark appears.

Microsoft 365 (Beta)

- Connecting a company: in Microsoft 365 › Tenants, a wizard registers the Microsoft apps that are needed, each
  with only the permissions of its use, takes you to give consent and checks the connection. Check says what is
  missing and how to fix it, and the credentials can be rotated. The RMM Defender connector can use this connection,
  with no secret to keep or renew, or keep its own app.
- View and manage: in Mailboxes and users, each company's people, mailboxes, groups, licenses, MFA and
  forwarding, kept up to date. Each person under management takes a seat of your NetPilot license (people can be left
  out of management); whoever is left without one shows "No seat" and NetPilot warns you.
- Actions with confirmation: block, sign out of sessions, reset the password, remove forwarding and
  "Compromised account", on one person or up to 20 at a time. Each one asks you to confirm your identity and is valid
  only for that action and those people. The temporary password is shown once and NetPilot doesn't keep it.
- SMTP forwarding: to see and remove the forwarding that Microsoft only exposes through Exchange Online, NetPilot
  uses PowerShell 7.6 and an Exchange component that is downloaded or uploaded from Settings. The Docker images
  include PowerShell and the .deb package suggests it.
- People labels: NetPilot's own labels, with rules and a preview, to group people (for example, to choose what to
  back up). Protected labels ask you to confirm your identity, and whoever has limited access only labels the people
  they can see.
- Automations and policies: in Automations, rules that react to a new person, a risky account, a new external
  forward or a full mailbox: they notify, open a ticket or bring the backup forward, and propose blocking, signing
  out, removing a forward or preparing the onboarding, which a person confirms (blocking and onboarding can become
  automatic if a Microsoft 365 administrator confirms it, and they never act on administrators). In Policies:
  MFA registered, No external forwarding, Recent sign-in, Mailbox quota and Label requirements, each with
  its status.
- Compliance: the Microsoft 365 checks join those of ISO 27001, ENS and NIS2. The assessments you already had pick
  them up the next time you press Run checks, without losing what you had answered.
- Microsoft 365 backups: in Microsoft 365 › Backups, mail, calendar and contacts of the mailboxes, OneDrive
  (with its versions), shared mailboxes and SharePoint libraries, to a target in Backups › Targets, every 6 hours by
  default (from 1 hour to 7 days). Only what you choose is backed up: person by person, in bulk or by label. Each
  person backed up takes a seat of their own, apart from the endpoints'; shared mailboxes and sites don't. You can
  browse, download as a ZIP (.eml, .ics, .vcf and files) and restore, always to a new folder named
  "Restaurado <date>", without overwriting anything, to the person's own mailbox or OneDrive or, with the
  Microsoft 365 admin permission, to another person's in the same connection. Copy now brings a backup forward and
  Forget deletes what was backed up for a person. Teams arrives in 1.8.6.
- Permissions and license: Microsoft 365 is a license module, with one counter of people for management and
  another for backups, and it doesn't need RMM. It has its own permissions, none granted by default, in
  Administration › Permissions (the same editor as RMM › Permissions). Its notifications only reach the people
  allowed to see what they refer to, in the bell, by email, push or WhatsApp, and the "no seats left" ones go to
  unrestricted administrators. Every screen has its help.

Security awareness (Beta)

- Simulated phishing campaigns against your own staff: you choose whom, the template and the landing page, and
  NetPilot sends the emails in the window you set, according to the site's time zone. A second person approves
  campaigns with their own content; those from the library don't need it. Every send respects each person's
  departments, and nothing personal travels in the links. Programs create a campaign by themselves every month or
  quarter, with the difficulty going up.
- People and domains: people come from Microsoft 365, an LDAP directory (always with TLS) or a file, and emails
  only go to the company's own domains: those verified in its Microsoft 365 or those you prove with a TXT record. A
  temporary DNS failure doesn't count a verified domain as lost: it only stops being valid when DNS says its TXT
  record is gone.
- Sender: simulations go out through a sender used only for them, with its own simulation domain and DKIM,
  directly or through a dedicated relay, never through the company's Exchange Online or NetPilot's notification mail.
  Before each company's first campaign you must pass Test delivery, and Check DNS looks at the sender's records
  (see "Keep in mind").
- Library: 18 simulation emails and 18 landing pages per language, in three difficulty levels, and 6 short courses
  with a quiz, in Spanish and English. None uses real brands, companies or people.
- Training and scores: whoever falls for a simulation sees a page explaining what happened and can be assigned a
  course. Courses, from the library or the company's own, come with reminders and, on passing, a PDF certificate with
  a code anyone can check. Scores by person, department and campaign respect privacy: whoever lacks permission to see
  names only sees grouped data, and queries with names are recorded in a log.
- Report: an Outlook add-in, Microsoft's button and a reports mailbox collect what staff report, and NetPilot
  matches it with the simulations.
- Reports and dashboard: the Awareness Dashboard and its card on NetPilot's Dashboard; organization and
  campaign reports and the evidence for Compliance, in PDF and Excel, on demand or scheduled every month or quarter
  (without names by default); and an adjustable data retention.
- License and public pages: Security awareness is another license module, with seats, and it also works without
  RMM or Microsoft 365. Its public pages (links, landing, training and reports) live at an address of their own, the
  public host, isolated from the rest of NetPilot, and without the license they don't answer. The public host is
  checked by itself every day: if DNS fails one day, links keep working, nothing is paused and it is checked again the
  next day; if DNS doesn't answer for more than three days in a row, it stops being valid for scheduling, its
  campaigns are paused and NetPilot raises a notification. Security awareness notifications only reach whoever has a
  permission of the section.

Backups: fixes and improvements

- Images with VSS: the system image on Windows accepts the devices VSS gives, cleans up what it leaves behind and
  no longer repeats useless attempts. If VSS fails, the file backup still goes on without a snapshot, but it says so
  with the reason Windows gave, and retries once after 30 seconds if the failure is temporary.
- NAS over SMB: if two targets on the same NAS use different accounts, NetPilot warns you when saving, and a
  backup waits up to 15 minutes for the connection to be freed instead of failing. If it still clashes, the warning
  says the server, the account and who holds it. If the endpoint lacks cifs-utils, the panel says so before backing
  up and offers Install cifs-utils.
- NAS credentials rejected: if the NAS password or user stops working, or the account lacks permission, the daily
  check leaves the target as "Access denied" and warns, just like Test, instead of leaving it "Unreachable".
- Store app aliases (WindowsApps): they no longer show as "Read error"; they are saved without a warning and not
  recreated on restore (with an agent older than 1.8.5, the restore gives "The link was not restored" on them: it is
  harmless). A special file that Windows won't let you read because a component is missing shows its own warning.
- Warnings and counters: identical warnings appear together, with how many times and when, also in earlier runs.
  "New" shows "—" when it isn't known, "Not consistent" gives its reason on hover and a backup "With warnings" shows
  "Finished", not "Succeeded".
- Where the time goes: the run shows pauses apart, a live time left and the real "Upload" to the target. On S3,
  "Uploaded" now counts what really goes out, indexes included, and can be somewhat larger than before.
- Bandwidth limit: it now also slows images, except those going to a disk on the endpoint itself. With a low
  limit, an image takes longer than in 1.8.4.
- Interrupted backup and window: a backup paused because the window closed continues by itself in the next one
  without taking a seat while it waits; one that comes back with the window open no longer continues if it had been
  told to close (it ends canceled) or if something stops it: it waits, and its card says why. If it can't continue for
  7 days because its policy, section or seat is missing, it closes by itself.
- Random start times: the spreading counts endpoints, not backups: the file backup and the image backup of the
  same endpoint, or those of an endpoint already backing up or restoring, no longer delay backups that fit, and when
  they don't fit, an endpoint's two backups go out together at their time.
- Key kit: when downloading the kit of the key in use, targets whose read user predates 1.8.5 change to
  "Your kit carries access to this target", and each target with a reader shows the state of its kit on its card.
- In progress and why it waits: the endpoint's Backups tab shows at the top what hasn't finished and the next
  backup, and Runs has the "In progress" quick filter. Every waiting backup says why (no seat, another backup or
  restore of the same endpoint, the endpoint offline…) and when it goes out. The random delay only applies when not
  all of them fit at that time, and a backup paused because the endpoint is off no longer takes a seat.
- Delete this damaged backup: a "Damaged" backup is deleted from its menu in the endpoint's Backups tab and can be
  recovered for a few days.
- Testing an SMB target tells apart "Resource not found", "No route to the target", "Connection refused" and
  "No answer in time", and warns about DFS paths, which the server doesn't follow: enter the real server and share.
  "No maintainer" says why there is no relay and leads to choosing one.

What changes

- Departments: the notes, attachments and history of an object also follow the departments rule. A user with both
  a limit of locations or companies and one of departments can neither see nor touch the notes, attachments or history
  of an IP or circuit from another department, and what they can't see answers the same as what doesn't exist. In
  Field work, that circuit's card appears without notes or photos and read-only, and a user limited by locations or
  companies can no longer save a note or label text on something they can't change (for example, a cable that goes to
  another site). The same rule applies in the change log, the activity, the dashboard, the 30-day chart, the
  assistant, the audit report and the provider circuits, and the assistant no longer names a site you can't see.
- Help requests: they now follow the site, company and departments of their endpoint, in the list, the counter,
  the card, the timeline and the notifications. Whoever doesn't have "View help requests" stops receiving their
  notifications; whoever is limited by site or company receives those of their sites (before, none).
- Silence alerts and planned changes: with limited access you can only silence the alerts of specific endpoints
  you see; windows by location or for the whole network, and saved ones that touch endpoints you don't see, are left
  to whoever sees everything. An "In progress" change only silences the endpoints seen by whoever starts it (one
  started before 1.8.5, with that person's current limits). Whoever approves a request that cites objects they don't
  see gets the notice "This request cites objects you do not see" and can approve it anyway.
- Linux installer: updating (also from the panel), repairing and uninstalling only use the configuration the
  installer itself keeps, and if its state file is missing, updating stops and explains how to continue instead of
  rebuilding it with default values. The address the server listens on is checked before it is written into the
  service (0.0.0.0, "::", an IP or a host name): if the saved one isn't valid, it stops being used, NetPilot listens
  on 0.0.0.0 (or on 127.0.0.1 with local access or behind a proxy) and the installer says so. Updating with PostgreSQL
  keeps the database password, also with spaces or "+", and an old login name that isn't valid no longer prevents it.
  The service account can no longer be root, only root can read the backup made before deleting, and the installer log
  now lives in /var/log/netpilot-installer (the log viewer finds it there and in the old folder).
- .deb package: purging it (apt purge) removes what the installer keeps for itself and keeps the data and the
  configuration; removing or purging it no longer hangs if the server configuration file is damaged, and once removed
  (apt remove), NetPilot is no longer taken for a package installation when updating from the panel.
- Patches on PostgreSQL: approving or rejecting a patch in RMM no longer gives an error on PostgreSQL (on SQLite,
  the default database, it didn't fail).
- The assistant no longer gives an error when asked about recent changes by someone with access limited to a
  company without sites.

Keep in mind

- Microsoft 365 and Security awareness haven't been tested with a real tenant yet, only with a simulated
  Microsoft, DNS and SMTP. Start with a test company: register the apps, give consent, press Check and launch a
  campaign to a single person before opening it to everyone. Some parts depend on what your Microsoft 365 allows: SMTP
  forwarding needs Exchange Online, and Microsoft's live changes need a public HTTPS address.
- License: using these sections needs a license that includes Microsoft 365 or Security awareness, with their
  counters; Enterprise includes them all. Current licenses keep working, but they don't include them.
- Agents: the Backups improvements need this version's agent. Agents 1.8.3 and 1.8.4 update themselves according
  to their agent policy (you can bring it forward from the Agent versions card in RMM › Agents), and those of
  1.8.2 or older are moved once with Move to 1.9, which, despite its name, installs this server's version (1.8.5).
  With an older agent, the Backups screens look as before, without the new data.
- Teams backups: they arrive in 1.8.6. Some screens already show Teams parts (the "Backups · Teams" and
  "Restore · Teams" apps with their privacy notice, the Teams seat counter and the Teams license filter): the app can
  be set up and tested with Check, but a job doesn't let you choose Teams yet.
- Security awareness sender: it is only checked when you press Check DNS (there is no daily check yet). If DNS
  doesn't answer, the sender stays as it was, nothing is paused and the check shows in amber,
  "DNS could not be queried"; it only turns "Failing" when DNS says a record doesn't exist or its value doesn't match.
- Microsoft 365 backups: the NetPilot server writes them, so the target must be reachable from it (a NAS that only
  one endpoint can reach won't do), and the company's backup key must be active. After the first backup, each pass
  over a folder with changes takes longer the more emails it holds (with tens of thousands it can take more than a
  day): start with small mailboxes and check in Microsoft 365 › Backups how long it takes.
- Windows things not yet seen on real machines: VSS, SMB connections and aliases are built and tested, but haven't
  been seen on real machines yet. Run a restore test before relying on a backup.
- Going back from this version: if the database is downgraded, what 1.8.4 doesn't understand is lost, that is,
  everything in Microsoft 365 and Security awareness (connections, people, labels, jobs, campaigns, training and
  scores), and the RMM Defender connector that used the Microsoft 365 connection is left without it. What is on the
  targets isn't touched.
- Manual: the PDF manual is still the 1.8 edition and doesn't cover Backups, Microsoft 365 or Security awareness;
  the in-app help already does.

Coming in the next versions (this may change)

- 1.8.6 beta, Endpoint condition and Backups. Each endpoint's color, with its reason and its alerts; easier and
  more complete endpoint backups (a new menu, protecting in four steps, restoring by what you want to get back,
  choosing what is backed up, backups that resume and run faster, a recovery USB with a graphical screen); Teams
  backups, and an easier-to-read change log.
- 1.8.7 beta, VPN and labels. NetPilot's own VPN: access to the panel, the agents' VPN, users and rules, and
  tunnels between sites. In the Warehouse: batches and expiry dates, direct printing on Zebra and TSC printers, and
  redirectable QR codes.
- 1.8.8 and 1.8.9 beta, security and cloud. The installation's security sets itself up when installing and can be
  reviewed later, and NetPilot on a cloud server reaches all its agents and backups.
- 1.8.10 and 1.8.11 beta, reports and cybersecurity. One place for reports and dashboards, Cybersecurity (with
  Compliance, Risk and Exposure) and the new menu with filters.
- 1.8.12 and 1.8.13 beta, tickets. Complete tickets: templates when asking for help, history, reassign, reply,
  notes and statuses.
- 1.9.0, the final version: the complete manual and the move to the stable channel.
